organization: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Office of Productivity and Technology
public_contact_or_submission: public contact form published on the OPT site
why_relevant: publishes the official labor and total factor productivity series and the methods behind them; the natural venue for a ground-versus-channel question about the measurement itself
notes: use the published public contact form, not personal staff addresses

organization: BLS Productivity and Costs news release
public_contact_or_submission: public release and linked technical notes and tables
why_relevant: shows revision practice directly, for example second-quarter 2026 nonfarm business productivity revised up 0.7 percentage point; a checkable example of a reading that changes with source data
notes: comments go through the public channels on the release, not to named economists

organization: BLS Office of Productivity and Technology errata and data corrections
why_relevant: a public, opt-in route for pointing out a measurement problem in a published series; a ground-visible correction channel
notes: corrections are about the data, not about the Tether framework

public_contact_or_submission: public program page and published open calls for proposals
why_relevant: explicitly funds research on re-engineering official economic statistics and on measuring technical change; proposals considered on a rolling basis; a venue whose purpose is exactly the ground-versus-channel question
notes: use the published open call, not personal emails of co-directors

organization: NBER Conference on Research in Income and Wealth (CRIW)
why_relevant: long-standing venue where measurement researchers present checkable work; public programme rather than a private list
notes: check current call for papers before submitting

organization: NBER Productivity, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship program
why_relevant: topic-matching working group for the generative half of the question, the import and absorption of new general-purpose technologies
notes: public programme page; no personal contact data listed here

organization: American Economic Association, Journal of Economic Perspectives
public_contact_or_submission: public submission guidelines page with the journal's own institutional address
why_relevant: JEP prefers two to five page proposals and explicitly welcomes suggestions for topics and symposia; suitable for a short shape-plus-refuter note rather than a full theory
notes: the address on the page is the journal's institutional one; the journal note says most articles are solicited and unsolicited material gets a brief reply

why_relevant: the J-Curve paper appeared here, making it the topical venue for an import-and-composition-lag version of the claim
notes: linked from the AEA journal menu; check current submission rules before use

why_relevant: cross-country series let the slot-level pattern be checked outside a single national statistical system; an independent frame for triangulation
notes: listed as a mapping aid and public data source; use public data access routes only
